approach: In drain.rs, `run_job` asks `athena_core::disk::is_environment_reason(&run.reason)` on a run that did not pass and is not needs-accepting/held. If true it pushes the job line as before and returns a new non-failure `RunStep::Environment`. `attempts` maps that to a new `ItemEnd::Environment`, returned before `failures += 1`. `finish` notes the item as left queued and calls `pass_over` with the run's reason, and the worker takes the next item. Two real failures still reach `ItemEnd::Failed`. The module docs and CHANGELOG say so. The same test also covers the steward's per-class `repeated_failures` count: it skips jobs whose outcome reason is an environment stop, using the same classifier, and a steward test covers that. display.rs needs no change. A drain test uses the existing `Stub` with one new scripted field.

decisions.choice: Classify with `athena_core::disk::is_environment_reason` (backed by `StopCause::of`) on `run.reason` inside `run_job`; add no list to athena-cli.
decisions.reason: disk.rs documents itself as the one place that says which closing reasons are environment stops, and the scope guard and `athena retry` already use it. A new kind of stop is then added once, in disk.rs, and the drain follows.

rejected.option: Match 'environment:' or the reason strings in drain.rs
rejected.why: A second list. The request forbids it, and it would miss the older unprefixed 'the producer did not complete: ... 401' form that `StopCause::of` handles.

rejected.option: Classify inside `Steps::run` (the real implementation) and add a field to `Run`
rejected.why: Changes the Steps trait and every stub in tests/drain.rs. The reason is already in `Run.reason`, so the drain can classify it itself.

decisions.choice: On an environment stop the item ends for this run (new `ItemEnd::Environment`). It does not take its second attempt, and it is passed over like Held/Waiting.
decisions.reason: The request says the item stays queued for a later run. An immediate retry would hit the same expired login or full disk, spend money, and be read as one more failure.

rejected.option: Skip the failure count but still retry in the same run
rejected.why: Retries into the same environment fault and burns budget. A later run is the stated behaviour.

rejected.option: Stop the whole drain on an environment stop
rejected.why: The request says the run goes on to the next item.

decisions.choice: Change steward.rs `repeated_failures` to skip jobs whose `outcome.reason` is an environment reason, with a steward test. Leave display.rs unchanged.
decisions.reason: The steward count feeds the model a 'repeated failure' signal, and counting a login-expired job there is the same fault. The fix is one extra `is_environment_reason` check against the same classifier. display.rs only formats Stop::RepeatedFailure after the drain has set it, so it needs no change.

rejected.option: Leave steward.rs alone and only record why
rejected.why: Cheap, but it leaves the same mislabel in the steward's input. The change is one line and testable.

rejected.option: Edit display.rs to add text for the new case
rejected.why: The pass-over line and the note already show the reason. No new Stop variant exists, so there is nothing for display.rs to format.

risks.risk: An expired login now no longer stops the drain, so every remaining item may hit the same 401 and the run spends its budget.
risks.mitigation: The new item end returns before the failure count and is not retried in this run. The item is passed over once per run via pass_over, so a persistent fault (for example an expired login) makes the drain walk the whole queue and fail each item once. That cost is bounded by the budget and the job limit, and each item is retried in a later run, as the request asks. The docs say so.

risks.risk: A real failure could be taken for an environment stop (the classifier also matches any 'environment:'-prefixed reason).
risks.mitigation: Classify only the exact reason of a run whose outcome is not passed, needs-accepting or held, using the shared classifier. The test pairs a rejection with a work-failure reason ('checks failed' or 'ended rejected') and still expects RepeatedFailure.

risks.risk: The steward change reaches beyond the drain and changes the model's input.
risks.mitigation: The steward change is one filter on the same classifier, with a test for both cases. If a reviewer rejects it, revert that file; the drain fix stands alone.

risks.risk: Adding a field to `Stub` breaks the many tests that build it.
risks.mitigation: The new field defaults to empty, and Stub derives Default. Other tests with their own `Steps` impls are untouched.

demonstrations.method: Run the new test through the public `drain::drain(&stub, limits(5.0), &Quiet)`. Stub items a and b; outcomes [Rejected, Landed, ...]. `a` runs and is rejected, `reread a` makes a-retry, and a-retry ends in an environment stop. Assert: stop is not RepeatedFailure and failed_item is None; the log has `run a-retry` and then `read b`, `run b`, `land b`; report.landed == 1; report.queued holds a; a note says a is left queued; the job line for a-retry carries the reason.
demonstrations.observes: The run does not stop at a; it goes on to b and lands it, and a stays queued with its reason.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new RunStep/ItemEnd mapping, the second attempt (a-retry, login expired) counts as failure 2 and ItemEnd::Failed sets Stop::RepeatedFailure naming a. The test's assert_ne!(report.stop, Stop::RepeatedFailure) fails, as does the check that the log reaches `read b`, `run b` and `land b`.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `drain::drain` with guards `stop_requested`, budget and `paused`. The seam is the `Stub` implementing `Steps` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, injected as the first argument. It exists today. Step 3 adds one field, `environment_stopped: Vec<&'static str>`, which makes `Stub::run` return `Run { outcome: Some(Failed), reason: format!("{PRODUCER_AUTH}: ...") }` for those jobs. The stub only scripts the reason; the classification and the item-end logic under test stay in drain.rs.

demonstrations.method: Run the two existing tests unchanged through `drain::drain`. The first has two rejections ('ended rejected'); the second has a run that passes and a landing that fails twice. Both must still end with Stop::RepeatedFailure naming a, which shows the classifier does not swallow ordinary failures.
demonstrations.observes: Both tests pass: two real failures still stop the run.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the change counted every failure as an environment stop, or dropped the failure count, these tests would not see Stop::RepeatedFailure with failed_item `a`. Their reasons are 'ended rejected' and 'checks failed', which are not environment reasons.

open_questions: Whether the read path should be treated the same way. A reader that fails on an expired login yields `read.error`, and `run_job` then returns RunStep::Failed with read false and that error as its reason. The plan classifies only run reasons, as the request says ('attempt ends in an environment stop'). The producer may add the same check on the reader's error text if the real reader reports the prefix; this was not verified.

Does 'network' have a reason in the shared classifier? `StopCause` lists low disk, check timeout, producer 401, usage limit and any 'environment:'-prefixed reason. I saw no network-specific constant, so a network stop counts only when its reason carries the 'environment:' prefix. Changing the classifier is out of scope.

Whether `Run.reason` from the real `Steps::run` carries the closing reason of the job for an environment stop. The reading says yes (line.reason is set from run.reason at drain.rs:1515); I did not read the real `Steps::run` implementation.
